key_insight: Indoor photovoltaics, energy storage, and low-power neuromorphic computing should be co-designed so edge AI nodes can run reliably on harvested local energy instead of centralized infrastructure.
engineering_relevance: The paper frames a practical route to sustainable distributed intelligence by pairing high-efficiency indoor solar harvesting with ferroelectric materials that can improve both energy buffering and compute efficiency.
method: Review requirements for indoor photovoltaics in distributed intelligence
Assess emerging materials against energy-harvesting and storage needs
Argue for (anti)ferroelectrics as enablers of electrostatic storage and in-memory computing
evidence_signal: This is a perspective article, so its support comes from a requirements-based synthesis of the literature rather than new experimental data or benchmark results.
watch_item: System-level deployment still depends on matching intermittent indoor power output with real device energy demand, durability, and scalable fabrication.
paper_title: Computing at the Edge Enabled by Indoor Photovoltaics and Ferroelectrics
